# Split change — family-balanced → §35 regime holdout (fixall Phase 1)

**What changed:** `data/features/split_assignment.csv` regenerated by the new single producer `scripts/make_split_assignment.py` (`dataset_version` v1.0 → v1.1). The default `split` column is now the **regime holdout**: TEST = whole scenario regimes `E_rapid_subsidence` + `E_accelerating_subsidence` + `E_stable_ground` (never seen in train/validation); VALIDATION = deterministic 1-in-5 within each remaining family (no rng); the rest is TRAIN. The legacy 60/20/20 family-balanced assignment is preserved as the second column `split_family_balanced`. The synthetic CSVs are byte-unchanged (same seed 42); only the split changed. The old per-event assignment stays retrievable at git tag `pre-fixall`.

**Class support (windows) in the regime holdout:** test = 5,625 NORMAL / 5,625 WARNING / 5,625 CRITICAL; validation = 11,250 / 2,718 / 657; train = 45,000 / 10,539 / 2,961. Test support is balanced by construction; validation CRITICAL support is thinner (657) but nonzero.

**Why stable_ground is held out for test:** §35 demands an unseen-regime test split, but the two pure growth regimes alone produce a test set with **zero NORMAL windows** — the alert engine's `P(WATCH or higher)` and the §24 false-alarm family would be undefined. Holding out the no-deformation regime as well keeps the test honest AND fully supported. This makes the test *harder* (NORMAL is scored on unseen ground too), not easier.

## Ablation A–F (test split, arm by arm) — old vs new

| arm | PR-AUC old | PR-AUC new | F1 old | F1 new | Brier old | Brier new |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A_sensors_only | 0.494 | 0.845 | 0.453 | 0.772 | 0.110 | 0.588 |
| B_add_temporal | 0.512 | 0.671 | 0.430 | 0.488 | 0.070 | 0.374 |
| C_add_spatial | 0.472 | 0.655 | 0.412 | 0.483 | 0.062 | 0.351 |
| D_add_vibration_health | 0.483 | 0.677 | 0.400 | 0.448 | 0.063 | 0.344 |
| E_add_physics | 0.483 | 0.604 | 0.398 | 0.462 | 0.056 | 0.573 |
| F_add_sentinel1 | 0.487 | 0.619 | 0.400 | 0.462 | 0.057 | 0.559 |

**Reading (state the direction, not a spin):** RANKING improves on the regime holdout (PR-AUC up in every arm; F1 up in every arm) — separating anomalous from normal windows generalises across regimes. CALIBRATION collapses (Brier 0.056 → 0.573 at arm E): the model never trains on the rapid/accelerating probability scale, so its P(CRITICAL) on unseen regimes is systematically wrong. This is the textbook regime-shift signature and is exactly what §35's "unseen parameter regime" wording asks the prototype to expose. The old numbers were the easier measurement; both are preserved (old: `git tag pre-fixall`, `experiments/ablation_a_to_f.json` history; new: current files).

## Sepetra report (regenerated under the regime holdout)

| metric | old (family-balanced) | new (regime holdout) |
|---|---|---|
| accuracy | 0.890 | 0.437 |
| F1 (binary alert) | 0.398 | 0.462 |
| recall (binary alert) | 0.443 | 0.582 |
| ROC-AUC (CRITICAL vs rest) | 0.982 | 0.687 |
| PR-AUC (CRITICAL vs rest) | 0.901 | 0.455 |
| Brier (P-CRITICAL) | 0.0558 | 0.5729 |

Accuracy drops because the test mix changed (one third of the new test set is the unseen no-deformation regime and the model over-warns there); recall and F1 *improve*; ranking halves; calibration degrades as above.

## End-to-end pipeline (regenerated `experiments/pipeline_run.json`)

| stage/output | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| test windows scored | 18,000 | 16,875 |
| predicted NORMAL/WARNING/CRITICAL | 13,346 / 3,211 / 1,443 | 10,158 / 6,042 / 675 |
| alert ladder GREEN/WATCH/WARNING/CRITICAL | 14,994 / 1,668 / 878 / 460 | 10,094 / 2,133 / 4,596 / 52 |

The ladder still fires end-to-end (§35 bullet 8 demonstrated on held-out data), but reaches CRITICAL far less often — the engine's evidence conditions rarely all hold on unseen regimes. Honest note: with calibration degraded (above), the low CRITICAL count reflects the calibrative gap, not a safer system.

## Domain-gap Stage 2 (synthetic → tabletop rig)

Old (model trained under family-balanced): max P(CRITICAL) 0.868, 24 windows above the alert threshold, WARNING recall 0.029. New (regime holdout): max P(CRITICAL) 0.188, zero windows above threshold, WARNING recall 0.098, confusion NORMAL 10,355 / WARNING 3,496+380. **The rig-domain transfer gets worse under the more honest split** — the transferred model no longer trains on the extreme-magnitude regimes that the rig's signals resemble. `reports/domain_gap.md`'s standing conclusion (ranking transfers, operating point does not) still holds; the numbers in that report are the old-split ones and are labeled as such by the git tag.

## Temporal forecasting (notebook 06) — verdict REVERSED

| horizon | old MAE skill vs persistence | new MAE skill vs persistence |
|---|---|---|
| next_window (1 step) | **+32.5%** (neural justified) | **−193.1%** (neural MAE 22.67 vs persistence 7.73) |
| hours_6 (4 steps) | **+50.9%** (neural justified) | **−18.8%** (neural MAE 36.72 vs persistence 30.92) |

Under the regime holdout the LSTM **loses to persistence on every supported horizon** — it can no longer train on the growth regimes it is asked to predict, and its train distribution (slow/irregular growth + stable ground) extrapolates worse than the trivial baseline. The §16 "neural justifies its complexity" claim is therefore **withdrawn** for the regime-holdout evaluation; persistence remains the §16 baseline. This is the single largest metric reversal of the split change and is reported as-is (rule 8).

## Which split each artifact now uses

| artifact | split | file |
|---|---|---|
| §35 acceptance claims (default) | regime_holdout | everything keyed on the `split` column |
| Ablation A–F, IF ablation, notebooks 04/05/06/07/10, sepetra, pipeline | regime_holdout (regenerated this phase) | current JSON/notebook outputs |
| Pre-fixall numbers | family_balanced (original assignment) | git tag `pre-fixall` |
| Comparability control (nb07 §4) | both | `notebooks/07_validation_and_ablation.ipynb` asserts family-balanced val→test gaps stay small (leakage control) and reports regime gaps as the honest shift |

`dataset_manifest.json → split_definition` records producer, method, config key, counts and class support for both splits.
